question: If HCF and LCM of two rational numbers are equal, then the numbers must be
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know the relationship: **Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM**.

If **HCF = LCM = k**, then Product of numbers = **k × k = k²**.

Since **HCF** is the **highest common factor** and **LCM** is the **lowest common multiple**, the only way they can be equal is if the numbers themselves are **identical**.

**∴ The correct answer is Equal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** HCF(a, b) = LCM(a, b)

**Formula Used:** a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24d0337233a1c0cb75bfa96e399302306be871b8064f63c4304d673bd62f58d6.png] 

⇒ Let HCF(a, b) = L and LCM(a, b) = L.

⇒ We know that **HCF** always divides **LCM**, and **HCF ≤ Numbers ≤ LCM**.

⇒ If **HCF = LCM**, then the range between the factor and the multiple collapses to a **single value**.

⇒ This implies a = L and b = L.

⇒ Therefore, **a = b**.

**∴ The correct answer is Equal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule

For any two positive integers a and b, **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are **co-prime** if their **HCF is 1**. Their LCM is simply the product of the numbers.

HCF and LCM Relation

The **HCF** of any set of numbers is always a **factor of their LCM**.</p
